summary: Defines an information model for PSAMP, listing the data items used to encode sampled packet data and details about the sampling process. It builds on the IPFIX information model and extends it for packet sampling reports.

plainLanguage.summary: When a router samples packets, it has to say what it sampled and how it made that choice. This document defines the vocabulary for that: the name and number of every data item, from the identifiers of the selection process to the bytes of the sampled packet, the timestamp of the observation and the accuracy of any estimate derived from the sample.

questions: what is the psamp information model
how do psamp and ipfix relate
subtitle: The dictionary of data items a router uses to report which packets it sampled and how it picked them.

tldr.problem: Packet sampling needs a standard way to describe and export sampled packet data and the sampling process, and the existing IPFIX information model did not cover everything PSAMP Reports need.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 5477 defines extra Information Elements, starting at ID 301, for selectors, sampling and hash settings, timestamps, packet sections and statistics. PSAMP Reports are exported with IPFIX.
tldr.outcome: Exporters and Collectors share one vocabulary for sampled packets. It is a Proposed Standard and the unit metadata lists no replacement.

today: RFC 5477 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2009. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is the information model that the PSAMP protocol in RFC 5476 uses.

sections.title: What the Document Covers
sections.content:
Packet sampling techniques are required for various measurement scenarios, and the Packet Sampling protocol provides mechanisms for packet selection using different filtering and sampling techniques. A standardized way to export and store the Information Elements that describe the sampled packet data and the sampling process is required, and this document defines that information model.

The definition of the PSAMP information and data model is based on the IPFIX information model in RFC 5102, because the PSAMP protocol is built on IPFIX, and the PSAMP protocol document RFC 5476 specifies how to use the IPFIX protocol in the PSAMP context. The document examines the IPFIX information model and extends it to meet the PSAMP requirements, so its structure follows the IPFIX document closely.

The main part of the document, Section 8, lists the Information Elements to be transmitted by the PSAMP protocol, and Sections 5 and 6 describe the data types and Information Element properties used, and their relationship to the IPFIX information model. The Information Elements already described by the IPFIX information model are used by PSAMP where applicable, and only those that are not already described there are defined here.

The PSAMP charter specified no requirements for measuring packet errors such as drops or malformed packets, and this document does not cover such data. If there is a need to collect and export packet error information, the appropriate Information Elements can be requested from IANA and exported with the PSAMP protocol.

The body of Section 8 was generated from an XML document, which is attached in Appendix A. The XML-based specification can be used to check the specification for syntactic correctness and, together with the IPFIX information model, for automated code generation, and the resulting code can be used in PSAMP implementations to handle processing of PSAMP Information Elements. The body of Section 8 is normative, while the appendix is informational.
sections.plainLanguage: The document is a dictionary. It names every value a router can report about a sampled packet and about the sampling process, and gives each one a number so that both ends of the export agree on what is meant. It also carries a machine-readable version of the same list.

sections.title: The PSAMP Documents and the Relationship to IPFIX
sections.content:
This document is one of a series from the PSAMP group. RFC 5474, A Framework for Packet Selection and Reporting, describes the framework for network elements to select subsets of packets by statistical and other methods and to export a stream of reports on the selected packets to a collector. RFC 5475 describes the set of packet selection techniques supported by PSAMP. RFC 5476 specifies the export of packet information from a PSAMP Exporting Process to a PSAMP Collecting Process. This document defines the information and data model for PSAMP.

A PSAMP Report can be seen as a very special IPFIX Data Record: it represents an IPFIX Flow containing only a single packet. The IPFIX information model can therefore be used as a basis for PSAMP Reports. Nevertheless, PSAMP Reports need properties that the current IPFIX information model cannot express, and this document describes the extensions to the IPFIX information model that allow the information and data required by PSAMP to be modeled. Some of these extensions allow the export of what may be considered sensitive information.

The PSAMP Information Elements are defined in accordance with Sections 2.1 to 2.3 of the IPFIX information model, and the document strongly recommends defining the optional units property for every Information Element where it applies. The data types of the IPFIX information model are also used for the PSAMP Information Elements, which MUST be constructed from the basic abstract data types and data type semantics described there; the data types are not repeated in this document, and their encoding is described in the IPFIX protocol.

Information Elements SHOULD NOT be overloaded with multiple meanings or reused for multiple purposes, and a different Information Element SHOULD be allocated for each requirement. Although the presence of certain other Information Elements allows the selection method to be inferred, a separate Information Element is provided for the selectorAlgorithm so that it can serve as scope for the Selector Report Interpretation. Even when Information Elements are specified with a particular selection method in mind, they are not restricted to that method and MAY be used for different selection methods in the future.

The PSAMP Information Element identifiers were initially started at value 301, in order to leave a gap for ongoing IPFIX work that requires new Information Elements. It is expected that this gap in the numbering will be filled by IANA with new IPFIX Information Elements.
sections.plainLanguage: PSAMP is a family of documents: one describes the framework, one the selection techniques, one the wire protocol and this one the data. A PSAMP report is really an IPFIX record about a flow of one packet, so the IPFIX model does most of the work and this document fills the gaps with new data items.

sections.title: Describing the Selection Process
sections.content:
The Information Elements in this section describe the sampling configuration of a selection process, and all have the data type semantics of an identifier or a quantity.

The selectorAlgorithm Information Element, identifier 304, identifies the packet selection methods applied by the selection process, such as filtering or sampling. Most of these methods have parameters, and further Information Elements are needed to specify packet selection with those methods and all their parameters. The registry of methods is maintained by IANA, and new assignments are subject to Expert Review. The document defines eight methods: systematic count-based Sampling, with the parameters samplingPacketInterval and samplingPacketSpace; systematic time-based Sampling, with samplingTimeInterval and samplingTimeSpace; random n-out-of-N Sampling, with samplingSize and samplingPopulation; uniform probabilistic Sampling, with samplingProbability; Property Match Filtering, which currently has no agreed parameters; and three hash-based filtering methods, using BOB, IPSX or CRC, which share the hash parameters.

The samplingPacketInterval element, 305, specifies the number of packets that are consecutively sampled, so a value of 100 means that 100 consecutive packets are sampled. It is measured in packets. The samplingPacketSpace element, 306, specifies the number of packets between two samplingPacketIntervals: a value of 100 means that the next interval starts 100 packets, which are not sampled, after the current interval is over. It is measured in packets.

The samplingTimeInterval element, 307, specifies the time interval in microseconds during which all arriving packets are sampled, and the samplingTimeSpace element, 308, specifies the interval in microseconds between two such periods, a value of 100 meaning that the next interval starts 100 microseconds after the current one is over, during which no packets are sampled.

The samplingSize element, 309, specifies the number of elements taken from the parent population for random sampling methods, and the samplingPopulation element, 310, specifies the number of elements in that population; both are measured in packets, and together they describe a random n-out-of-N selector.

The samplingProbability element, 311, specifies the probability that a packet is sampled, expressed as a value between 0 and 1, with the same probability for every packet. A value of 0 means that no packet was sampled, because the probability is 0.
sections.plainLanguage: One element names the selection method, and the rest give its settings: how many packets in a row to take and how many to skip, how long to take them for and how long to pause, how many to take out of how many, and the chance of taking any given packet. The method names are kept in a registry that IANA maintains.

sections.title: Hash-Based Selection Parameters
sections.content:
Nine Information Elements describe the configuration of the hash-based selection methods. The individual parameters are explained in more detail in the PSAMP selection techniques document.

The digestHashValue element, 326, specifies the value produced by the digest hash function, and the hashIPPayloadOffset element, 327, specifies the IP payload offset used by a hash-based selection selector, with hashIPPayloadSize, 328, specifying the IP payload size used by it. The hashOutputRangeMin element, 329, and the hashOutputRangeMax element, 330, give the beginning and the end of the hash function's potential output range.

The hashSelectedRangeMin element, 331, and the hashSelectedRangeMax element, 332, give the beginning and the end of the range of the hash output that has been selected, so that packets whose hash falls inside that range are the ones chosen.

The hashDigestOutput element, 333, contains a boolean that is true when the output of the hash selector has been configured to be included in the packet report as a packet digest, and false otherwise. The hashInitialiserValue element, 334, specifies the initialiser value given to the hash function.
sections.plainLanguage: The hash methods pick packets by hashing part of each packet and keeping the ones whose hash falls in a chosen range. Nine elements describe that setup: where in the payload to hash, how much, the seed, the range of hash values that counts as selected, and the full range the hash could produce.

sections.title: Packet Data Elements
sections.content:
Four Information Elements report raw content of a packet, and all of them may also be used in IPFIX. If the values for those sections vary for different packets in a flow, the flow report contains the value observed in the first packet of the flow.

The ipHeaderPacketSection element, 313, which may have a variable length, carries a series of octets from the start of the IP header of a sampled packet. With sufficient length it also reports octets from the IP payload, subject to the IETF policy on wiretapping, and the size of the exported section may be constrained by limitations in the IPFIX protocol. The ipPayloadPacketSection element, 314, also of variable length, carries a series of octets from the start of the IP payload of a sampled packet. The IPv4 payload is the part of the packet that follows the IPv4 header and any options, which RFC 791 calls the data or data octets, and the IPv6 payload is the rest of the packet following the 40-octet IPv6 header, with any extension headers considered part of the payload.

The mplsLabelStackSection element, 316, carries the first n octets from the MPLS label stack of a sampled packet and, with sufficient length, octets from the MPLS payload. The mplsPayloadPacketSection element, 317, carries the first n octets from the MPLS payload of a sampled packet, that is, the data that follows immediately after the MPLS label stack.

The size of an exported section may be constrained by limitations in the IPFIX protocol, and the data for all four of these fields MUST NOT be padded.
sections.plainLanguage: Four elements carry the bytes themselves: the start of the IP header, the start of the IP payload, the start of the MPLS label stack and the start of the MPLS payload. Each one is a chosen length, and the exported section may be shorter than the packet because of the limits of IPFIX.

sections.title: Statistics and Confidence in the Reported Numbers
sections.content:
Seven Information Elements report statistics from the metering process. The selectorIdTotalPktsObserved element, 318, specifies the total number of packets observed by a selector for a specific value of SelectorId, and the selectorIdTotalPktsSelected element, 319, the total number of packets selected by it. Both are measured in packets and both should be used in an Options Template scoped to the observation they refer to.

The absoluteError element, 320, specifies the maximum possible measurement error of the reported value of a given Information Element, and it has the same unit as the Information Element it accompanies, so the real value of the metric can differ by that amount, positive or negative, from the measured value. The relativeError element, 321, expresses the same thing as a percentage of the measured value. Both provide only the error for measured values. If an Information Element holds an estimated value that comes from sampling, the confidence boundaries and confidence level have to be provided instead, using the upperCILimit, lowerCILimit and confidenceLevel elements.

The upperCILimit element, 336, specifies the upper limit of a confidence interval and is used to give an accuracy statement for an estimated value. The confidence limits define the range in which the real value is assumed to be with a certain probability p, and the limits always need to be associated with a confidence level that defines that probability. The document notes that a confidence interval only provides a probability that the real value lies within the limits, which means the real value can lie outside them. The lowerCILimit element, 337, gives the lower limit, and the confidenceLevel element, 338, gives the probability that the real value lies within a given range.

All three of upperCILimit, lowerCILimit and confidenceLevel are required to specify confidence and should be disregarded unless all three are given together. They should be used in an Options Template scoped to the observation they refer to.
sections.plainLanguage: Some of the numbers are counts and some are estimates, and the report says which. A count comes with a maximum error; an estimate comes with a lower limit, an upper limit and the probability that the true value falls between them. The three confidence values only mean anything together.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The PSAMP information model itself does not directly introduce security issues. Rather, it defines a set of attributes that may, for privacy or business reasons, be considered sensitive information.

Exporting values of header fields may make attacks possible for the receiver of the information that would otherwise only be possible for direct observers of the reported flows along the data path. For that reason, the Information Elements pertaining to packet sections MUST target no more than the packet header, some subsequent bytes of the packet, and encapsulating headers if present. Full packet capture of arbitrary packet streams is explicitly out of scope, per the IETF policy on wiretapping.

The underlying protocol used to exchange the information described here MUST therefore apply appropriate procedures to guarantee the integrity and confidentiality of the exported information. Such procedures are defined in separate documents, specifically the IPFIX protocol document.
sections.plainLanguage: The model itself is not a security risk, but the values in it can be sensitive, since header fields can tell an observer about traffic that was otherwise visible only on the path. The packet elements are therefore limited to the header and a few following bytes, and the transport has to protect the export.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The PSAMP information model has two sets of assigned numbers. As the PSAMP protocol uses the IPFIX protocol, the IANA Considerations section of the IPFIX information model document governs the assignments of numbers used in the protocol and in the information model.

This document specifies an initial set of PSAMP Information Elements fulfilling the needs in the PSAMP selection techniques document, as an extension to the IPFIX Information Elements. The PSAMP Information Element IDs were initially started at value 301, in order to leave a gap for any ongoing IPFIX work requiring new Information Elements, and it is expected that this gap in the numbering will be filled by IANA with new IPFIX Information Elements.

Each new selection method MUST be assigned a unique value in the selectorAlgorithm registry, and its configuration parameters, along with the way to report them with an Options Template, MUST be clearly specified. The initial content of the registry is given in the sampling configuration section of this document. New assignments are administered by IANA and are subject to Expert Review, with a group of experts checking the Information Element definitions against the existing ones for completeness, accuracy and redundancy. That group is initially drawn from the chairs and document editors of the IPFIX and PSAMP working groups.
sections.plainLanguage: Two sets of numbers are handed out: the identifiers of the data items, which start at 301 to leave room for IPFIX, and the identifiers of the selection methods. New methods get a new number, and the people who review them check that no two elements mean the same thing.
